commands.result_summary:
1	# Diagnose - Investigate failed BPMN runs
2	
3	Capability index for post-run investigation.
4	Diagnose owns the diagnostic priority ladder for BPMN Process Orchestration runs: incidents, runtime variables,
5	deployed BPMN asset correlation, element executions, cursors, generated package metadata, and traces.
6	
7	> **Where you came from / where to go next.** Diagnose is downstream of Operate (a debug or deployed run failed, hung,
8	> or behaved unexpectedly) and points back to Author for source fixes.
9	> Running and lifecycle live in [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../operate/CAPABILITY.md);
10	> source fixes live in [registry-workflow.md](../registry-workflow.md).
11	>
12	> **Inherits universal rules from [SKILL.md](../../SKILL.md).** BPMN source is model-authored; generated package files
13	> and Integration Service enrichment are CLI-owned.
14	> Use `uip maestro bpmn ... --output json` for diagnostic reads and redact private runtime data in summaries.
15	
16	## When to use this capability
17	
18	- Triage a failed debug or deployed process run.
19	- Read incidents and faulting element IDs.
20	- Inspect runtime variables and element executions.
21	- Fetch the deployed BPMN asset when local files may differ.
22	- Map runtime failures back to BPMN source and generated package metadata.
23	- Identify failures caused by unresolved Integration Service enrichment, bad bindings, missing diagrams, invalid mappings,
24	  or stale package files.
25	- Decide whether the safe next action is retry, cancel, migrate, cursor movement, re-authoring, package regeneration,
26	  or cloud configuration repair.
27	
28	## Critical rules
29	
30	1. **Investigate in priority order** - context, incidents, runtime variables, deployed BPMN asset,
31	   element executions/cursors, generated package files, then traces. For failed
32	   BPMN run triage, always execute the deployed asset read
33	   `uip maestro bpmn instance asset <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json`
34	   before writing the diagnosis, even when incidents and variables already
35	   reveal the likely root cause.
36	2. **Always include folder context on instance and incident reads** - `instance` commands require `--folder-key` or `-f`,
37	   and `incident get` requires `--folder-key`.
38	3. **Use the CLI as the diagnostic interface** - run `uip maestro bpmn ... --output json` reads. When mock or fixture
39	   files are present in a test harness, treat them as CLI backing data and do not read those files directly unless you
40	   are explicitly debugging the mock harness.
41	4. **Fetch deployed BPMN when local source may differ** - do not assume the working tree matches what ran.
42	5. **Map failures to BPMN element IDs** - use IDs to identify the source node, gateway, event, sequence flow,
43	   or extension that needs Author work.
44	6. **Separate runtime symptoms from ownership of the fix** - BPMN structure and mappings belong in Author;
45	   Integration Service enrichment and generated JSON come from CLI generation;
46	   folder/process/release choices belong to cloud configuration.
47	7. **Do not expose private runtime data** - redact tenant, user, connection, folder, URL, payload,
48	   and secret values in summaries.
49	8. **Do not mutate while diagnosing** - retry, cancel, migrate, and cursor movement are Operate actions and require
50	   explicit user consent after root cause analysis.
51	
52	## Workflow
53	
54	| Journey | Read |
55	| --- | --- |
56	| Triage a failed run | [references/troubleshooting-guide.md](references/troubleshooting-guide.md) |
57	| Recognize recurring failure patterns | [references/failure-modes.md](references/failure-modes.md) |
58	
59	## Common tasks
60	
61	| I need to... | Read these |
62	| --- | --- |
63	| Find the faulting element | [references/troubleshooting-guide.md](references/troubleshooting-guide.md) |
64	| Compare local and deployed BPMN | [references/troubleshooting-guide.md](references/troubleshooting-guide.md) |
65	| Inspect runtime variables, cursors, or element executions | [references/troubleshooting-guide.md](references/troubleshooting-guide.md) |
66	| Diagnose binding or generated JSON issues | [failure modes](references/failure-modes.md), [project layout](../shared/project-layout.md) |
67	| Diagnose Integration Service runtime issues | [failure modes](references/failure-modes.md) |
68	| Decide whether retry is safe | [troubleshooting guide](references/troubleshooting-guide.md), [manage guide](../operate/references/manage.md) |
69	| Fix the source | [registry-workflow.md](../registry-workflow.md) |
70	
71	For Integration Service enrichment details, read
72	[registry-workflow.md](../registry-workflow.md).
73	
74	## Anti-patterns
75	
76	- **Never start with verbose traces when incidents are available.**
77	- **Never call runtime lifecycle commands while diagnosing.** Diagnose reads; Operate mutates after explicit consent.
78	- **Never assume local BPMN is the deployed asset.**
79	- **Never retry before root cause is known.**
80	- **Never paste private incident payloads or connection details into docs, commits, or issue comments.**
81	- **Never patch generated package files as the only fix for a BPMN source defect.**
82	
83	## References

1	# Troubleshooting Guide
2	
3	Use this priority ladder for failed or misbehaving BPMN runs.
4	
5	> **Read-only boundary:** this guide diagnoses.
6	> Retry, cancel, migrate, and cursor movement are Operate actions and require explicit user consent after root cause is known.
7	>
8	> **Folder context:** `uip maestro bpmn instance ...` commands require `--folder-key <FOLDER_KEY>` or
9	> `-f <FOLDER_KEY>`.
10	> `uip maestro bpmn incident get` requires `--folder-key <FOLDER_KEY>`.
11	
12	## Step 1 - Confirm context
13	
14	Collect public-safe identifiers:
15	
16	- Process or package name.
17	- Instance/job ID.
18	- Folder/context label.
19	- Approximate run time.
20	- Local commit or package version, if known.
21	- Whether the run came from `uip maestro bpmn debug` or `uip maestro bpmn process run`.
22	
23	Do not record secrets, tenant URLs, connection IDs, or payload data in public notes.
24	
25	If you only have a deployed-process job key, start with:
26	
27	```bash
28	uip maestro bpmn job status <JOB_KEY> --folder-key <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
29	```
30	
31	Parse the instance ID, folder context, process key, final status, and any trace/run identifiers from the JSON output.
32	For debug runs, prefer the `instanceId` returned by
33	`uip maestro bpmn debug` and inspect it with `debug-instance` commands. Keep
34	deployed-instance status reads and debug-session inspection separate.
35	
36	## Step 2 - Read incidents
37	
38	Find the incident category, message, and faulting BPMN element ID.
39	If multiple incidents exist, start with the first root fault and avoid chasing downstream cancellation noise.
40	
41	```bash
42	uip maestro bpmn instance incidents <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
43	uip maestro bpmn incident get <INCIDENT_ID> --folder-key <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
44	uip maestro bpmn incident summary --output json
45	```
46	
47	For process-level incident overview:
48	
49	```bash
50	uip maestro bpmn processes incidents <PROCESS_KEY> --output json
51	```
52	
53	## Step 3 - Inspect runtime variables
54	
55	Inspect variables around the faulting element.
56	Redact private payloads.
57	Check whether expected outputs were missing, malformed, or literal strings instead of evaluated expressions.
58	If the user reports a behavioral mismatch, inspect variables even when the final
59	run status is `Completed`; a completed run only proves control-flow completion,
60	not semantic correctness.
61	
62	```bash
63	uip maestro bpmn instance variables <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
64	uip maestro bpmn instance variables <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --parent-element-id <ELEMENT_ID> --output json
65	```
66	
67	For affected elements, confirm runtime inputs and outputs match the modeled
68	contract before changing source.
69	
70	## Step 4 - Correlate deployed BPMN
71	
72	Fetch the deployed BPMN asset when local source may differ. Compare:
73	
74	- Faulting element ID.
75	- Root variables and mappings.
76	- Binding expressions.
77	- Integration Service extension content.
78	- Diagram and sequence-flow structure when the failure is import or package related.
79	
80	```bash
81	uip maestro bpmn instance asset <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
82	```
83	
84	For failed-run triage, always run this deployed asset command before the final
85	diagnosis, even when earlier incident and variable reads already explain the
86	failure. The deployed asset proves which BPMN definition actually ran and keeps
87	the priority ladder observable in command logs.
88	
89	Use the incident's faulting element ID to locate the BPMN element in the deployed asset first, then compare to local
90	`.bpmn`.
91	If they differ, diagnose what actually ran and treat local edits as a future fix, not as the executed definition.
92	
93	## Step 5 - Inspect element executions and cursors
94	
95	Element executions and cursors show where the runtime moved before it faulted or hung:
96	
97	```bash
98	uip maestro bpmn instance element-executions <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
99	uip maestro bpmn instance cursors <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
100	```
101	
102	Use these to distinguish a modeling problem from a runtime-state problem:
103	
104	- Activity fault: inspect the activity's inputs, mappings, extension payload, and upstream variables.
105	- Gateway stall: inspect outgoing sequence-flow conditions, default flow, and variable values.
106	- Event wait: inspect message/timer configuration, subscriptions, and whether the expected external signal exists.
107	- Subprocess or call activity fault: identify the child dependency, but do not invoke sibling skills automatically.
108	
109	## Step 6 - Check generated package files
110	
111	If the failure is binding, entry point, package, or runtime metadata related, inspect generated JSON:
112	
113	- `bindings_v2.json`
114	- `entry-points.json`
115	- `operate.json`
116	- `package-descriptor.json`
117	
118	Generated-file mismatch usually means Author should fix BPMN or rerun CLI generation/enrichment.
119	
120	Correlate package files to the deployed BPMN:
121	
122	- `entry-points.json` should reference the intended BPMN file and start event.
123	- `bindings_v2.json` should contain generated resources required by executable resource and connector elements.
124	- `operate.json` should identify the intended main file/runtime metadata.
125	- `package-descriptor.json` should include BPMN and generated JSON files under `content/`.
126	
127	## Step 7 - Pull traces last
128	
129	Use verbose traces only when incidents, variables, deployed asset, and package files do not explain the issue.
130	
131	```bash
132	uip maestro bpmn job traces <JOB_KEY> --output json
133	```
134	
135	## Output
136	
137	Return a concise diagnosis:
138	
139	- Faulting element ID.
140	- User-visible symptom.
141	- Likely root cause.
142	- Whether the fix belongs in BPMN source, CLI enrichment, generated package files, or cloud configuration.
143	- Safe next action.
144	
145	## CLI command reference
146	
147	```bash
148	uip maestro bpmn job status <JOB_KEY> --output json
149	uip maestro bpmn job traces <JOB_KEY> --output json
150	uip maestro bpmn instance get <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
151	uip maestro bpmn instance incidents <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
152	uip maestro bpmn instance variables <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
153	uip maestro bpmn instance variables <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --parent-element-id <ELEMENT_ID> --output json
154	uip maestro bpmn instance asset <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
155	uip maestro bpmn instance element-executions <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
156	uip maestro bpmn instance cursors <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
157	uip maestro bpmn incident get <INCIDENT_ID> --folder-key <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
158	uip maestro bpmn incident summary --output json
159	uip maestro bpmn processes incidents <PROCESS_KEY> --output json
160	```
161	
162	Lifecycle commands are intentionally absent from this diagnostic command list.
163	Use [operate/references/manage.md](../../operate/references/manage.md) only after the diagnosis supports a
164	side-effecting action and the user consents.
165

parameters.content:
# Incident Diagnosis — inst-triage-001 (folder-public)

ROOT_CAUSE_ELEMENT: ServiceTask_FetchInvoice
ROOT_CAUSE_CATEGORY: BindingResolution

## Evidence

- `uip maestro bpmn instance incidents inst-triage-001 -f folder-public --output json`
  returned two incidents:
  - `inc-root-001` — sequence 1, element `ServiceTask_FetchInvoice`, category
    `BindingResolution`: "Resource binding failed to resolve; the element could
    not start."
  - `inc-noise-002` — sequence 2, element `ServiceTask_PostToLedger`, category
    `UpstreamDependencyFailed`, with `causedBy: inc-root-001`: "Element was
    cancelled because an upstream element (inc-root-001) never completed."
- `uip maestro bpmn incident get inc-root-001 --folder-key folder-public --output json`
  confirms the fault: a binding named `invoiceSource` failed to resolve at
  `ServiceTask_FetchInvoice`, so the element never started.
- `uip maestro bpmn incident summary --output json` confirms ordering:
  `firstFaultElementId: ServiceTask_FetchInvoice`, `firstFaultCategory:
  BindingResolution`, and explicitly notes "UpstreamDependencyFailed incidents
  are downstream consequences of the first fault."

## Conclusion

`ServiceTask_FetchInvoice` is the true root cause: its resource binding
(`invoiceSource`) failed to resolve, so the task could never start. The second
incident, on `ServiceTask_PostToLedger`, is downstream noise — it is explicitly
tagged `causedBy: inc-root-001` and categorized `UpstreamDependencyFailed`,
meaning the ledger-posting task was only cancelled because the upstream fetch
task it depends on never completed. It occurred four seconds later (sequence 2
vs. sequence 1) and carries no independent fault signal of its own; fixing the
binding at `ServiceTask_FetchInvoice` is the correct and sufficient remediation
target — `ServiceTask_PostToLedger` requires no separate fix.

# Incident Diagnosis — inst-triage-001 (folder-public)

ROOT_CAUSE_ELEMENT: ServiceTask_FetchInvoice
ROOT_CAUSE_CATEGORY: BindingResolution

## Evidence

- `uip maestro bpmn instance incidents inst-triage-001 -f folder-public --output json`
  returned two incidents:
  - `inc-root-001` — sequence 1, element `ServiceTask_FetchInvoice`, category
    `BindingResolution`: "Resource binding failed to resolve; the element could
    not start."
  - `inc-noise-002` — sequence 2, element `ServiceTask_PostToLedger`, category
    `UpstreamDependencyFailed`, with `causedBy: inc-root-001`: "Element was
    cancelled because an upstream element (inc-root-001) never completed."
- `uip maestro bpmn incident get inc-root-001 --folder-key folder-public --output json`
  confirms the fault: a binding named `invoiceSource` failed to resolve at
  `ServiceTask_FetchInvoice`, so the element never started.
- `uip maestro bpmn incident summary --output json` confirms ordering:
  `firstFaultElementId: ServiceTask_FetchInvoice`, `firstFaultCategory:
  BindingResolution`, and explicitly notes "UpstreamDependencyFailed incidents
  are downstream consequences of the first fault."

## Conclusion

`ServiceTask_FetchInvoice` is the true root cause: its resource binding
(`invoiceSource`) failed to resolve, so the task could never start. The second
incident, on `ServiceTask_PostToLedger`, is downstream noise — it is explicitly
tagged `causedBy: inc-root-001` and categorized `UpstreamDependencyFailed`,
meaning the ledger-posting task was only cancelled because the upstream fetch
task it depends on never completed. It occurred four seconds later (sequence 2
vs. sequence 1) and carries no independent fault signal of its own; fixing the
binding at `ServiceTask_FetchInvoice` is the correct and sufficient remediation
target — `ServiceTask_PostToLedger` requires no separate fix.
